Content & licence policy

Which games may appear on Toolstack Lab Games, and what we show you about each one.

What we list

Today every game on this site is made by Toolstack Lab: our own code, art and sound. If we list a game by someone else, such as an open-source classic, it must meet all of these rules:

  • Its licence is a permissive open-source licence (such as MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0 or zlib) or a public-domain dedication that allows commercial use and changes. Copyleft licences (GPL, CC BY-SA) and non-commercial licences are not listed for now.
  • Its maker, licence, original source and any changes we made are named on its game page, with the copyright notice the licence asks us to keep.
  • It runs on its own web address, separate from this site, inside a sandboxed frame.

What we never list

  • Games that infringe a trademark or copy art, characters, levels or other assets we have no rights to. A clearly-licensed open-source classic is fine, but it keeps its author's credit and is never named or presented as an official version.
  • Games that need an account or collect personal data just to play.
  • Store art or screenshots taken from other sites. Every picture here is a frame from the game itself or art we made.

How we vet games

A game is only published once its licence and source are on record. Both are shown on every game page and in the list on this page. A game without them cannot be published.

Your privacy

This site sets no cookies and loads no ad, analytics or other third-party scripts or fonts. Game progress is saved in your own browser and never leaves your device.

Questions or a problem?

If you think a game here breaks this policy, tell us through gettoolstacklab.com and we will review it.
